items.title: Is China Really Inferior to Other Countries?
items.content_html: Growing up, I always heard people complaining that China’s national conditions were inferior to America, Switzerland… and other countries, and so I grew up nourished by that kind of environment. China — in what way exactly is it inferior to foreign countries, or rather, where does the difference lie? This is a string of questions. Where do we find the answers? Growing up I learned that a country’s development is inseparable from the wisdom of the people at the bottom — creating things, building homes, running trade… and what is the basic precondition for all these activities? A stable and prosperous order. Yes, that’s the answer. I seemed to vaguely understand something… Flipping through history, our motherland’s growth must be analyzed from before and after 1840. What things were like before 1840, people today of course don’t know; all we can verify are the history books and materials left by past dynasties. Their credibility isn’t entirely high either, but they’re still quite useful for a broad historical review. The First Industrial Revolution began in England in the 1760s, that is, 1760. What was China doing in 1760? In 1760 China was in the twenty-fifth year of the Qianlong reign; Qianlong had just ascended the throne, and the country was in the middle of the Kang-Qian flourishing age, with everyone at peace and content. So why didn’t China enter the scope of the Industrial Revolution, or rather, why were there no machine inventions? That reason requires turning history back further. China’s Four Great Inventions originated in the Spring and Autumn period, the Eastern Han, the Sui-Tang, and the Northern Song respectively — that is, 476 BC, 25 AD, 581-907 AD, and 960 AD. Counting the time, there were gaps of a hundred years in between, but inventions did happen. During that time society was sometimes in turmoil, yet thought was extremely open, without entanglement over profit and glory (I guess it was roughly like that) — with a stable and open-minded way of thinking, inventions were inevitable. However, from the Sui dynasty came the imperial examination system, which the Tang further established, the Song perfected, and the Ming and Qing brought to flourish. Back then the imperial examination was for becoming an official, and becoming an official was for bringing glory to one’s ancestors — much the same goal as building a career today. Everyone thought of studying diligently for ten years, for one day of glory. Beyond the Four Books and Five Classics there was still only the Four Books and Five Classics, and thinking revolved around just these few places. Inventions therefore became fewer, and everyone was based in this way of thinking, quietly finishing one round after another. Lagging behind was thus unavoidable, and failing to keep up with the First Industrial Revolution was only natural. In addition, the Qing dynasty at the time restricted navigation and rejected foreign culture. The self-sufficient stability of the “Heavenly Kingdom” plus the ignorant indoctrination of the Four Books and Five Classics stripped away open-ended thinking. China only invented them, without bringing out their uses. And during this period the inventions flowed outward, while the Western world kept researching and improving, pushing the economy into a new era. We can put it this way: England began developing its economy in 1760. And China? Before 1840 it was still the most primitive economy; even by 1949, when the Republic of China was established, China’s economy still hadn’t. And America? It became independent in 1783, freed itself from British economic control in 1814, and vigorously developed its economy, encouraging invention and innovation. By 1860 the American economy had leapt to 4th in the world. And China? Jiaqing cut the troops, forbade going abroad. The Anglo-French allied forces entered Beijing, burned the Old Summer Palace, and the country was in turmoil. Then before 1949, China was in the middle of World War II, followed immediately by civil war. From the First Industrial Revolution to the founding of New China in 1949, China never had genuine economic development, nor any measures or inventions to revive the economy. Meanwhile America made a fortune off the war, and other countries too were in economic depression, shifted onto others by war. And today, more than half a century on, China’s economy is recovering at a rapid pace, is growing. None of us has any right to say China is bad, nor any right to say Chinese people are uncivilized. Did any country develop directly out of civilization from the very start? Any country that has developed its economy for half a century is already quite civilized. It’s true that we can’t compare with foreign countries in education, welfare, and social security — you can make your own choices, but you have no right to disparage your own motherland. This is a fact, and also a rule.

items.title: 国内不如国外吗
items.content_html: 从成长的时间里我总是听着别人去抱怨中国国情不如美国、瑞士……其他国家，于是我就跟着这种环境的滋养长大了。 中国，国内到底哪点比不上国外，又或者说差别在哪里？这是一连串的的疑问，这答案从哪里找到呢。 在成长中我知道，一个国家的发展离不开底层的人民智慧，创造事物，建设家园，经营贸易……这一切活动的基础条件又是什么？安定繁荣的秩序。对，这就是答案，我恍惚知道了什么…… 翻翻历史祖国的成长得从1840年的前和后来分析。 1840 年以前是什么样子，我们现在的人当然不知道，可考证的只有历代留下的史书、资料。可信度也并不完全大，而这对于大的历史回顾还是相当有用处的。第一次工业 革命开始于18世纪60年代的英国，也就是1760年。1760年的中国正在干什么？1760年的中国正是乾隆二十五年，乾隆刚刚登基，国内正处于康乾盛 世的时段，人人安乐太平。那为什么国内没有进入工业革命的范围或者说没有机器的发明？那这个原因又得把历史往前翻。 中 国四大发明分别起源于春秋、东汉、隋唐、北宋，分别是公元前476年、公元25年、公元581-907年、公元960年算算时间中途有过百年的差距，但是 发明还是有的。在这时间里，社会时有动荡，思想是极为开放的，没有利益与荣耀的纠葛（我猜大概这样）安定而又开阔的思维，有发明是必然的。然而，从隋朝出 现了科举制度，唐朝进一步确立，宋朝完善，明清兴盛。那时科举就是为了当官，当官就是为了光宗耀祖，和如今干一番事业也是差不多的目的。所有人都想着寒窗 苦读，一朝荣耀。除了四书五经还是四书五经，思维就在这几个地方转。发明也就少了，看所有的人都基于这种思维，安定走完一拨又一拨。 落 后也就难免了，没跟上第一次工业革命也很自然。另外当时的清朝是限制航海，排斥外来文化。正式天国自足的安定以及愚昧的四书五经教化，剥夺了开放式的思 维。中国只发明了他，去没有将他们的用途发挥出来。而这期间发明的外流，西方世界不断钻研的改进，使得经济进入一个新的历程。 我 们可以这样说，英国是从1760年开始发展经济的。而中国呢？1840年以前还是最原始的经济，即便是到了1949年中华民国成立，中国的经济依然没有。 而的美国呢，1783年独立，1814年摆脱英国经济控制，大力发展经济，鼓励发明创新。1860年美国经济跃居世界第4。而中国呢，嘉庆裁兵，禁止出 洋。英法联军入京，火烧圆明园，处于动荡中。 那1949年以前，中国正处在第二次世界大战中、紧接着是内战。从第一次工业革命到1949年新中国成立，中国没有过真正的经济发展，也没有什么振兴经济的措施和发明。而此时，美国打发横财、其他国家也是经济萧条靠战争被转移。 而 今，半个世纪多了中国经济在急速复苏，在成长。我们任何人没有资格说中国不好，也没有资格说中国人不文明。那个国家一开始都直接从文明发展过来的吗？那个 国家发展了半个世纪的经济就已经很文明了。我们是比国外的教育、福利、保障比不了，你可以有自己的选择，但是没有资格说自己的祖国。这是事实，也是规则。
